rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~96%, Jan follow-up ~58% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); BoC Dec ~80% (Reuters); BoE Dec ~82%; ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~85%; RBA Dec hold ~99%
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays all but certain, and the Fed's Beige Book survey gave no reason to doubt it. The stock slide made traders a little less sure about more hikes after that. Canada's central bank looks set to hike again, which is lifting the loonie.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US Q3 GDP +4.3% annualized, second estimate (fcst 3.5%); jobless claims 189K (fcst 201K); new home sales Oct 701K (fcst 650K); Beige Book 8 of 12 districts growing; Germany Q3 GDP +0.1% q/q final
rows.read: The US economy is still running hot, with growth revised up sharply and layoffs rare. Germany barely grew over the same months. That gap favors the dollar, though the stock slide is a new risk to US spending.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US core PCE Oct +3.3% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Beige Book: prices rising moderately, tariffs cited; Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y; BoJ core CPI 2.3%
rows.read: US core inflation edged up again in October, and firms in the Fed's survey said costs keep rising, with tariffs among the causes. Australian inflation is also climbing. Both keep their central banks from easing.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Nasdaq ~−4%, S&P 500 ~−3% by late morning, VIX near 34 (Yahoo Finance); USD/CHF −0.56%; gold day low ~$3,437, back near $3,560
rows.read: US shares fell hard as chip stocks kept sliding and the US proposed new tariffs, and money moved into US government bonds. The Swiss franc gained most, and gold won back its whole morning drop. The Aussie and kiwi held up better than feared once the dollar weakened.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil jumped on claims of attacks on a Saudi refinery and on tankers near Hormuz, which helps the Canadian dollar and hurts oil importers like Japan and the euro area. Gold's recovery takes some pressure off Australia's export earnings.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies: up to 15% EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland; up to 20% extra China; 25% India; 35% Vietnam; comments due Jan 5, hearings Jan 25 (USTR); S&P France review Fri Nov 27
rows.read: The US proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, hardest on China and Southeast Asia, but nothing takes effect before early 2027. For Europe, Japan and Switzerland the rates sit near caps in existing deals. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating on Friday.
